editorial.headline: The Bali Reality Behind Retail Clock and Watch Trading
editorial.standfirst: This activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet a permanent Bali moratorium prevents PMA registration there today.
editorial.body:
Retail clock and watch trading covers the sale of watches in their many forms: wristwatches, pocket watches, wall clocks, alarm clocks and bells. It also includes retailing parts for watches and clocks. The scope is straightforwardly commercial, centred on bringing timepieces and their components to retail customers, rather than describing a manufacturing or repair activity.

The activity is open across every listed business scale: micro, small, medium and large. Nationally, its PMA status is open, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. For founders considering a foreign-owned company, that is the national position: full foreign ownership is permitted for this retail activity.

Bali changes the practical answer. A foreign-owned company cannot register this activity in Bali today. At the large-business scale, OSS risk is classified as Low or Medium-Low across every stated scope, placing the activity within Bali’s permanent, island-wide moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. This is not a reduction in the national ownership ceiling; it is a Bali-specific block on PMA registration.

That distinction deserves to remain clear. The national rule says the activity is open and may be fully foreign-owned. Bali’s rule says that, because of its stated risk treatment at the large scale, PMA registration is blocked on the island. A founder can therefore read the national foreign-ownership position as genuinely open while still recognising that it does not create a current PMA registration route in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness does not create a current PMA registration route for this activity in Bali.
